annotations.title: A Priest for euer.
annotations.text: In two respectes Christ is a Priest for euer: ◦ in that from the first instant of his Incarnation he was, and remaneth a Priest, now also in heauen: and al other Priestes are his ministerial vicares, not successors. So that al priestly functions, which they doe, he by them doth the same, as the principal Priest. Wherupon saith S. Paul ( 1. Cor 4. ) So let a man thincke of vs, as of the ministers of Christ, and dispensers of the mysteries of God. Secondly Christ dayly offering Sacrifice by the handes of his Priestes, doth continually pacifie Gods wrath, in behalf of those sinners, for whom it is duly applied, euen to the end of the world. Wheras the Priesthood of Aaron, and of al others in the old Testament, ceassed by their deathes, both in the office, and in the effect.

notes.text: Christs Priesthood for euer both in function and in effect.

annotations.title: According to the order of Melchisedech.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> As Melchisedech, king of peace and iustice, without father, mother, or genealogie, expressed in holie Scriptures, or otherwise knowen to the world, was Priest of the Hieghest, offered bread and wine, an vnbloudie sacrifice; communicating with both Chananeites and Hebrewes, blessed Abraham, and tooke tithes of him and his subiectes: so Christ the true King of peace & iustice, without father of his humanity, without mother of his Diuinitie, the Sonne of God, of ineffable genealogie, borne of a virgin in his humanitie, the Priest of God, offereth Sacrifice ( not only bloudie on the Crosse, but also ) vnbloudie in the formes of bread and wine, continueth the same by the ministerie of other Priestes, maketh al nations parrakers therof, blesseth them and receiueth of them al dutiful and religious seruice, as of his subiectes.

notes.text: The resemblance of Christs and Melchisedecs Priesthood.
